name: HiTech
label: FXHE Records
lede: Three Detroit rappers put out 15 CDs, handed one to Omar S at his storefront, and were on a Coachella stage by 2025.

eras.title: Tired of just rapping
eras.text: Ghettotech is Detroit's fast, filthy mix of techno, bass and rap, and DJ Assault, DJ Godfather and DJ Snowflake are the names its kids grew up on. King Milo, Milf Melly and 47Chops each came up in the city's rap scene first, then decided the club was the job.

years.src: The FADER: The Rap Report · The FACE: Interview · Rolling Stone: HiTech Interview · Metro Times: How HiTech became · Ableton: HiTech
years.h: After a bunch of acid trips, three rappers quit just rapping
years.p: King Milo, Milf Melly and 47Chops were all working Detroit's underground rap scene. In Milo's house they started making something built to move people instead.
years.xp:
The origin story changes with the interview. The FADER has Milo and Melly meeting at a [[Babyface Ray|d82481ab-4f2e-4fd7-af2f-9dbaa38704da]] show, The FACE has Milo and Melly going to parties 47Chops threw before they officially met, and Rolling Stone has the three of them coming together through a party where Chops was DJing.

Metro Times has the pivot in Milo's words: "After a bunch of acid trips later we were tired of just rapping." It also notes the three went to different high schools before they met through music. Ableton describes the roles: Milo engineers and mixes, Melly pushes the sound forward, Chops is the DJ and historian.

years.src: Rolling Stone: HiTech Interview · The FADER: The Rap Report · Ableton: HiTech
years.h: 47Chops hands a demo to Omar S at his storefront
years.p: Omar S played it all summer, then signed the trio to his FXHE label.
years.xp:
According to Rolling Stone, 47Chops first met Omar S at a show at his storefront and passed along a demo tape. Omar S then "played that shit all summer", and signed them to FXHE Records.

Milo recalls the pitch as "put the turbo boosters on our back" and "let's bring Detroit home". Rolling Stone calls the FXHE release their self-titled debut EP.

years.src: The FADER: The Rap Report · Metro Times: How HiTech became
years.h: HiTech gets a proper FXHE release, with "Henny Runtz" on video
years.p: The self-titled debut that began as 15 CDs comes out on Omar S's Detroit label in summer 2022, per The FADER.
years.xp: Metro Times dates the debut to 2021 (the CD run); The FADER says it was re-released on FXHE in summer 2022. We use 2022 for the FXHE release.

years.h: A Thanksgiving show at Bruiser sets up the Loma Vista deal
years.p: Dart Parker, the A&R behind [[Danny Brown|960afc67-9c21-46dd-9c7f-ff2b509e3150]], found the group at the 2022 Bruiser Thanksgiving concert, per Metro Times.
years.xp: That meeting is where the Loma Vista story starts: Metro Times has the label signing them in 2024, after Parker's introduction.

eras.title: Détwat
eras.text: A 28-minute record that plays like an argument against sitting down. FXHE put it out in May, and by year-end Pitchfork had it at No. 29 and The FADER at No. 10.

years.src: The FADER: Song You Need · Ableton: HiTech
years.p: The first single from DÉTWAT has a video built from footage of the trio opening for NYC rapper MIKE.
years.xp: The FADER described it as rattling along "like listening to podcasts at 1.5 speed but cool". Milo told Ableton it was built with friend $quid and others in the room, and that he slammed the table through a hot mic for percussion.

years.src: Album of the Year: HiTech · The FADER: The Rap Report
yt: HiTech live at The Body Shop with FullBody Durag, early 2023
years.h: DÉTWAT comes out on FXHE on May 26
years.p: Pitchfork's Cameron Cook called it the best ghettotech rager in recent memory.
years.xp:
Album of the Year lists the date as May 26, 2023, and Pitchfork's review score as 7.4. Tracks include "ZOOTED", "BIRTHDAY PEARLS", "TEETEES DISPO" and "WHYYOUFUGGMYOPPS", per The FADER.

The FADER called it more hot-blooded, hysterical and unrestrained than the debut. The clip is a live set at The Body Shop, filmed early in 2023, before the record was out.

years.src: The FADER: The Rap Report · Rolling Stone: HiTech Interview
years.h: King Milo's plan for the dance floor
years.p: He tells The FADER the trio wants dancers dancing, not standing around. A Paris interview from the same year is below.
years.xp:
In the same FADER interview 47Chops said: "It's like we're creating some shit at a time where people is looking for some new shit." The FADER also notes they favour Detroit pioneers like DJ Assault and DJ Snowflake.

Rolling Stone adds that the group had already been playing guerrilla-style shows at protests over Atlanta's "Cop City" project. The video has Milo, Melly and Chops in Paris ahead of their first show there at Espace Niemeyer.

years.cap: The trio piled onto a toy fire truck, 2023
years.src: Album of the Year: Pitchfork's 50 Best · Album of the Year: HiTech · Kresge Arts in Detroit
years.h: DÉTWAT ends 2023 at No. 29 for Pitchfork, No. 10 for The FADER
years.p: Pitchfork's list sits it between Avalon Emerson's & The Charm (No. 30) and jaimie branch's Fly or Die Fly or Die Fly or Die ((world war)) (No. 28).
years.xp: The 7.4 is the score for the Cameron Cook review as listed at Album of the Year. Kresge Arts in Detroit also notes Rolling Stone coverage of the record.

eras.title: Loma Vista comes calling
eras.text: A Detroit arts fellowship, a new label and two new songs, with London, Paris and Brussels shows in between.

years.cap: The three Kresge Arts in Detroit fellows, 2024
years.src: Kresge Arts in Detroit · Metro Times: How HiTech became
years.h: Kresge Arts in Detroit names HiTech a 2024 fellow
years.p: It's the Detroit arts fellowship, and the Kresge page calls the three self-taught Detroit natives who joined forces after local success.
years.xp: Metro Times says the three went to different high schools before they met through music. Kresge's description is of the group that made the debut after local success.

years.src: Metro Times: How HiTech became · The FACE: Interview
years.h: Loma Vista signs them while the FXHE albums stay off streaming
years.p: Metro Times reports the 2024 deal, with Dart Parker introducing them. The FACE noted the two FXHE albums were not on streaming.
years.xp:
The FXHE albums were still off streaming when The FACE ran its London interview, which covered their London debut in the magazine's New Noise series.

The video is a full HiTech set at Boiler Room Chicago from the same year.

years.src: Le Guess Who? · Bandcamp: SHADOWREALM · Stereogum: Stream HiTech's
years.p: Le Guess Who? lists the single "SPANK!" from September 2024. Bandcamp dates the two-track SHADOWREALM release to November 26.
years.xp: HiTech played Le Guess Who? in 2024 at a Thursday night curated by Crystallmess. Stereogum named "Shadowrealm" with ZelooperZ as a highlight.

eras.title: Coachella, then the long festival run
eras.text: A sound built for club floors went on a Coachella stage in daylight, then onto festival bills across North America and Europe.

years.src: Larimar Media · DJ Mag: Recognise 083 · Metro Times: How HiTech became
years.h: HiTech take ghettotech to Coachella's Sonora stage in daylight
years.p: Larimar Media quotes Pitchfork calling it one of the weekend's two best sets.
years.xp: DJ Mag pointed out it was a daytime festival slot for a sound made for club floors. Metro Times reports rappers ZelooperZ and G.T., producer Fullbodydurag and dancer Queen Gabby joined them.

years.src: Stereogum: Stream HiTech's · Larimar Media · DJ Mag: Recognise 083 · Exclaim!
years.p: Fourteen tracks, most under three minutes. Stereogum's Tom Breihan called it full of "joyously fizzy high-BPM jams".
years.xp:
Guests include ZelooperZ and Na-Kel Smith; Stereogum also names Debby Friday, Larimar Media names George Riley. Milo told DJ Mag mixtapes are "for the culture".

Stereogum notes a 34-second comedy skit on the tracklist.

years.src: Larimar Media · Metro Times: How HiTech became
years.h: Glastonbury, Dekmantel and Roskilde fill the summer
years.p: Larimar Media also lists Movement, Outlook and Green Man across North America and Europe.
years.xp: Metro Times had them scheduled for Movement at Hart Plaza in Detroit on Monday, May 26, at 5:45 p.m. Melly told Metro Times about a stretch of flying to Paris on weekends while still working at FedEx.
